entries.page: The Platform Rules Bible, section 13 (Facebook); Phase 3: The Everywhere Engine; Revenue Calculator data
entries.what: The manual printed a follower and minutes bar for Facebook's Content Monetization program: 10,000 followers, 600,000 minutes viewed in 60 days, 5 or more videos. Those numbers were the retired In-Stream Ads bar. Meta's own creators pages say the program is invite-only and publish no follower or minutes threshold; creators register interest in the Professional Dashboard and Meta invites pages. The bible, the chapter, and the calculator data now say so. One dated Algorithm Watch entry from October 12 repeats the guides' numbers as a report of what guides said; it stands as published, and this entry is its correction.

The manual said Twitch's 70/30 Plus rate stops at $100,000 of subscription revenue and falls back to 50/50. Twitch removed that ceiling in January 2024, and the Plus Program has been open to Affiliates as well as Partners since May 2024. The bible now prints the uncapped rate.

entries.page: Phase 3: The Everywhere Engine; Phase 5: The Monetization Stack
entries.what: The manual said TikTok Shop affiliate links came with no follower minimum. In the US, earning from product links in videos and live takes 1,000 followers, and the bar differs by country. The no-minimum routes are a link-only account, which earns nothing from videos or live, and a shop's own bound accounts. The three places that printed the old line now print the real gate.

The manual printed Twitch's old Partner test: 75 average viewers with 25 or more hours on 12 unique days. Twitch retired that test in September 2025. The Path to Partner now asks for six streams on six unique days, each averaging 75 viewers, in the last 30 days and again in the 30 days before. The bible now prints the current test and names the old one as retired.

The checker's 2027 activity test passed its output leg only at five uploads in 90 days. The announced rule is two long videos or five Shorts, so a long-form channel with two to four uploads was told it had missed a leg it had passed. The checker now reads the rule as written.

The manual's copy was swept clean of em dashes, at the source, across every page, chapter, tool, and data file. The home became the manual's complete contents in the same pass. This entry opens the ledger, so the route has a worked example.

note: The manual's corrections ledger. Every correction the editors accept prints here as a dated line: what page, what it said, what it says now. Rendered on the Algorithm Watch page (what-changed.html) by scripts/build.py; newest first.
